n1: The node is bound to the right target and asks about the requested chalk transformation. The edited image shows a strong, image-wide drawn treatment—grainy, softened, sketch-like surfaces across the giraffes and setting—so the repeated complete/yes judgments have concrete visual support; the source and edit alone do not establish that the reference partial label is correct. Do not force partial merely to match the aggregate label. Improve the criterion’s operational distinction between partial progress and completion: assess whether the chalk-drawing treatment is consistently realized across the image, versus only visibly begun or unevenly applied, and cite the specific regions or residual photographic qualities supporting that distinction. Keep preservation of the scene separate from style completion. The five high-confidence, consistent traces indicate no transport, schema, dependency, or instability issue; investigate the reference-label disagreement as a possible criterion or reference ambiguity rather than treating it as evidence that the edit is absent.

The node’s criterion is broadly appropriate, but its repeated “yes” judgments conflict with the supplied aggregate reference of “partial.” Reassess the edited image against the source and the completion threshold rather than treating any chalk-like appearance as automatically complete: the image retains the giraffes and scene and shows substantial painterly, softened texture, but the evidence should establish whether the result reads as a chalk drawing throughout or only as partial stylization. Distinguish visible progress from full fulfillment using concrete image evidence, and calibrate the label accordingly; do not infer missing edits from the reference label alone. The five high-confidence, near-identical traces indicate a systematic criterion/binding issue, not transport or dependency failure (all executions are valid and complete).
